data.description:
# Intake Brief: Audit freshness invalidates only on this work item's own data change

## Problem statement

The audit freshness gate (`_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint`
in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) invalidates a stored audit when any
fingerprint component changes. The original formulation fingerprinted
**whole-repo** state (git HEAD sha + work-item description hash + Key Files +
whole-repo working-tree hash), so any commit or uncommitted/untracked change
anywhere in the repository — even one from an *unrelated* work item — invalidated
every stored audit and re-triggered the full audit pipeline.

**Observed failure (SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0):** audited "Ready to close: Yes" at HEAD
`310773d5`; afterwards an unrelated work item (SA-0MSQ026T3009QY2L) merged
`aaabdede` to dev, the fingerprint changed (`58947e06…` matched recomputation at
`310773d5` but not at `aaabdede`), the re-audit ran and blocked on the pre-flight
full-suite cache gate — a verified item stuck in review.

**Current state (2026-10-21, HEAD `fe85415a3`):** the whole-repo components have
**already been replaced** by per-touched-file scoping (SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P, done):
the payload is now `{path_states, description_hash, key_files}` where each
touched path contributes its committed state (blob hash at HEAD, else the latest
touching commit) plus its narrowed working-tree state. An unrelated commit or
working-tree change now invalidates **only if it touches a file in the item's
touched set** (commits referencing the item id + comment-recorded commit hashes +
Key Files). The whole-repo HEAD sha is no longer a component, and
`_resolve_working_tree_hash` no longer exists. The observed failure case is
therefore **no longer reproducible** with today's formula.

The remaining delta of this item is the **strict rule** recorded in the original
Q&A: "An audit is only invalidated if there is a change to this work item's data
AFTER the audit was created." That rule is stronger than the current
per-touched-file formula — it requires a fingerprint over the item's own data
only (title + description, which contains the ACs and Key Files), with **zero git
calls**, so even a committed/uncommitted change to a file this item touched does
not invalidate.

## Users

- Audit operators / automated dispatchers relying on `audit_runner.py` freshness
  short-circuit (SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT) to skip re-audits of unchanged items.

**User story:** "As an audit operator, I want a stored audit to remain valid
unless THIS work item's own data changes, so unrelated repository activity
(including changes to files this item happened to touch) doesn't invalidate my
audits."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_compute_content_fingerprint` is computed from the **work item's own data
   only** — the item's title + description (the description contains the ACs and
   the Key Files section, so `key_files` may remain in the payload as a
   deterministic derivative of it). The per-path git components (committed HEAD
   blob hashes, working-tree state) and the whole-repo HEAD component are
   **removed** from the fingerprint — **no git calls in the computation**
   (`_resolve_touched_files` / `_compute_path_fingerprints` are no longer used by
   the fingerprint). *(Producer decision 2026-10-21: proceed with the strict
   formula — recorded below.)*
2. A git HEAD move caused by ANY other work item's commit does **not** invalidate
   a stored audit of an item whose own data is unchanged. Regression test:
   fingerprint is stable when only the HEAD sha differs (item data identical).
3. Uncommitted and untracked working-tree changes do **not** invalidate a stored
   audit — **including changes to files the item itself touched** (stricter than
   the current per-touched-path formula). Regression test: fingerprint is stable
   across `git status --porcelain` / `git diff --name-only HEAD` differences and
   across touched-file edits.
4. A change to this item's own data (title / description / ACs / Key Files
   section) after the audit **does** invalidate and re-runs the pipeline (existing
   description/key-files fingerprint tests remain green).
5. Comments, status/stage/priority/assignee changes, and sortIndex changes do
   **not** invalidate (they move `updatedAt` but are not audited content). This
   also removes the current comment-recorded-commit-hash contribution to the
   touched set (SA-0MVAWFYKT002CQ3L) — the fingerprint must not depend on comments.
6. **Migration of legacy reports:** reports persisted before this change carry
   fingerprints computed with the git-inclusive formulas that cannot be recomputed.
   Version the fingerprint line (e.g. `Audit content fingerprint (v2): <hash>`)
   so legacy/unversioned lines are distinguishable; legacy/unversioned reports
   fall back to the existing time-gate floor (auditedAt vs updatedAt +
   `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_BUFFER_SECONDS`, plus the persist-write tolerance) — **no
   silent mass re-audit wave** of the existing in_review backlog. Document the
   one-time re-audit consequence for legacy items whose `updatedAt` moved after
   the audit, and its interaction with the pre-flight full-suite cache gate.
7. Dead code cleanup: after the simplification, remove the fingerprints-only
   git machinery no longer referenced elsewhere (verify each of
   `_resolve_touched_files` / `_compute_path_fingerprints` — those still used by
   the file-scope manifest and Phase 2 remain). `_resolve_working_tree_hash`
   (SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ) is **already removed**; `_resolve_audited_head` stays
   (still used by green-run attestation).
8. **Test migration (nothing silently dropped):** the existing per-touched-path
   invalidation tests (`test_fingerprint_changes_when_touched_file_committed_change`,
   `..._dirty`, `..._staged`, `test_tool_artefact_rewrite_invalidates`, the
   comment-contribution tests, `test_unrelated_commit_does_not_reauth`) are
   rewritten to assert the **new rule** rather than deleted; new/updated tests
   cover title-change invalidation, stability across touched-file edits, and the
   versioned-line legacy fallback to the time gate.
9. Documentation updated: `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (freshness-gate
   section, currently ~lines 248-318/579-594/699/816), `skill/audit/SKILL.md`
   (~lines 42/182-186/204-210), and the code docstrings on
   `_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint` /
   `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`. All fingerprint call sites that must keep
   working with the simplified formula: `_check_audit_freshness` (item gate),
   `_get_child_audit_verdict` + `_child_content_changed` (child reuse, LP-0MSQ32MF200675AR),
   `cmd_check_freshness` (read-only probe, SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI),
   `_run_remediation_loop` (ruff-config re-hash), `_phase_fetch_and_cq`,
   `_reaudit_budget_exceeded_children`, `_phase_children` (child audit persistence).
   **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes** — code
   comments/docstrings, README, and any wiki or docs-site entries that describe
   the freshness gate. Full project test suite passes with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Verdict semantics unchanged:** the rule is about *when an existing audit is
  reused*, never about what the audit concludes. `--force` still bypasses the
  gate.
- **Read-only:** the fingerprint change must not execute the test suite or make
  any pi calls.
- **No regression in the freshness skip:** items whose data is unchanged still
  short-circuit in seconds (SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT intent preserved); the read-only
  `check-freshness` probe and `isAuditFresh` (ship, SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI) keep
  working.
- **Fail-open preserved:** any failure to compute the new fingerprint still falls
  through to a full re-audit (existing behaviour).
- **Child reuse gate:** child-audit reuse uses the same fingerprint — it must keep
  working with the simplified formula (children's own data unchanged → reused).

## Existing state

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`:
  - `_compute_content_fingerprint` (line ~2412) — payload =
    `{path_states, description_hash, key_files}` (per-touched-path, SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P).
  - `_check_audit_freshness` (line ~1950) — content gate primary; time gate
    (60 s + persist-write tolerance ~30 s) floor for fingerprint-less legacy
    reports; persistence-write tolerance covers the runner's own writes
    (SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM).
  - `_extract_content_fingerprint` (line ~2073) — parses the unversioned line.
  - `_resolve_touched_files` (line ~2213), `_compute_path_fingerprints`
    (line ~2336) — the per-touched-path git machinery this item's strict rule
    removes from the fingerprint (verify remaining uses: file-scope manifest at
    ~5224/7964/10897).
  - `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX = "Audit content fingerprint: "` (line ~1112,
    unversioned); embedded at ~5721/5747/6172 (persist) + re-extracted by the gate.
  - Call sites of the fingerprint: `_check_audit_freshness` (~2020),
    `_get_child_audit_verdict` (~6606), `_child_content_changed` (~7009),
    `cmd_check_freshness` (~2117/2120), `_phase_gate` (~9466),
    `_run_remediation_loop` (~10171), `_phase_fetch_and_cq` (~10357),
    `_reaudit_budget_exceeded_children` (~10786), `_phase_children` (~11380/11516/11918).
  - `_resolve_working_tree_hash` — **already removed** (SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ
    component replaced by per-path state); `_resolve_audited_head` (~2852) stays.
- `skill/audit/tests/` — tests split across files; fingerprint/freshness coverage
  lives mainly in `test_audit_runner_freshness.py` (1336 lines:
  `TestTouchedFileResolution` ~190, `TestContentFreshnessGate` ~348 — incl.
  `test_fingerprint_payload_keys_exclude_global_head`, touched-file invalidation
  tests, `test_unrelated_commit_does_not_reauth`, comment-hash tests) and
  `test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py`. Some existing tests assert the
  per-touched-path invalidation behaviour that this item reverses
  (`test_fingerprint_changes_when_touched_file_committed_change` /
  `..._dirty` / `..._staged`, tool-artefact invalidation, comment-contribution
  tests, `test_child_content_changed_fresh_survives_unrelated_head_movement` —
  these must be updated to the new rule).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — freshness-gate section ~lines 248-254
  (content gate + time gate + fail-open), 292/309-318 (child reuse), 579/594
  (inherited pass / child reuse), 699/816 (Phase 2 child reuse).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — freshness-gate summary ~lines 42, 182-186, 204-210.
- Related (separate repo, out of scope): herdr downtime worker's dispatcher-side
  `isAuditFresh` (ContextHub `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`, time-based
  `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`) caused the re-dispatch that exposed this;
  covered by RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT (ContextHub worklog). The ship-side
  `isAuditFresh` consumption is SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI (done) and stays in scope
  only as a consumer that must keep working.

## Desired change

Change `_compute_content_fingerprint` to hash only the work item's own data —
`{title, description_hash}` (Key Files parse from the description; explicitly
admit `key_files` in the payload or rely on `description_hash` as the ACs allow)
— with a versioned fingerprint line so legacy unversioned reports fall back to
the time-gate floor. Remove the per-path git components and the now-unused git
machinery from the fingerprint path; keep `_resolve_audited_head` for green-run
attestation; keep every consumer (item gate, child reuse, read-only probe,
remediation re-hash, child persistence) working against the simplified formula.
Update the fingerprint/freshness tests and both docs files to the new rule.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_compute_content_fingerprint`
  (simplify to item-data-only), `_check_audit_freshness` / `_extract_content_fingerprint`
  (versioned-line handling), `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`, dead-git-
  machinery removal, docstrings
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` and
  `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py` — update
  fingerprint/freshness tests to the new rule
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — freshness-gate section
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — freshness-gate summary lines

## Related work

- `SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P` — Audit freshness: re-audit only when files touched by
  the work item changed (**done**, 2026-09-28) — implemented the per-touched-path
  formula currently in the code; this item's strict rule goes further (item-data-
  only, zero git). **The original observed failure is already fixed by this item.**
- `SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ` — Include working-tree state in the audit content
  fingerprint (**done**, not in_review as the original brief stated) — the
  whole-repo working-tree component this item's rule REMOVES (superseded; the
  per-path state it inspired is also removed by this strict rule).
- `SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT` — Audit: content-based freshness gate (**done**) —
  introduced the fingerprint; this item simplifies its scope.
- `SA-0MVAWFYKT002CQ3L` — Stabilise child freshness fingerprint comments
  (**done**, 2026-10-21) — comment-recorded commit hashes feed the touched set;
  this item's rule removes the comment dependency (AC5).
- `SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI` — Ship: consume persisted audit content fingerprint
  (**done**) — read-only `check-freshness` probe consumer that must keep working.
- `SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0` — Audit runner: detect proxy 'cheap' mode (**done**) —
  the item whose blocked re-audit exposed this problem.
- `WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT` — RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item
  (ContextHub worklog) — dispatcher-side re-dispatch trigger; separate concern,
  out of scope.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "this work item's data":** title + description (ACs + Key Files
  section). Comments, lifecycle fields, and repo state are NOT audited content
  and must not invalidate.
- **Assumption — migration via versioned line:** legacy/unversioned reports fall
  back to the time gate (existing floor for fingerprint-less reports). A legacy
  item whose `updatedAt` moved after its audit is re-audited once, then stores a
  v2 fingerprint and is immune to comment/HEAD/working-tree churn thereafter.
  Accepted: this is a one-time, bounded transition.
- **Risk — stale code evidence (now broader):** dropping the per-path git
  components means a stored audit may reference code that changed under it — not
  just via another work item's Key-File edit, but **any committed or uncommitted
  change to a file this item touched** (the protection deliberately added by
  SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ and kept by SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P, with tests asserting the
  invalidation). Accepted by design — producer confirmed option (a) on
  2026-10-21 (comment SA-C0MVIAGIQU003WW4P); the audit's verdict remains the
  record for the item's own data.
- **Scope-creep risk:** reversing the per-touched-path design re-touches the
  child-reuse gate, the read-only probe, and the ship-side `isAuditFresh`
  consumer. Keep those as consumers that must keep working — do not extend the
  item to re-design them.
- **Risk — herdr re-dispatch noise:** herdr may still dispatch /skill:audit for
  items whose `updatedAt` moved; with this fix the runner short-circuits
  ("Skipping: audit still fresh", zero pi calls). Dispatcher-side change is out
  of scope (RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should a git HEAD move from another work item invalidate this item's audit?
  — Answer (user): No. "An audit is only invalidated if there is a change to
  this work item's data AFTER the audit was created." The rule is that simple.
- Q: What about the working-tree component (SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ)? — Answer:
  remove it too — same reasoning (repo state, not item data). This item
  supersedes SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ's component.
- Q: Do comments / status / stage changes invalidate? — Answer (assumed, per
  rule): no — they are not this item's audited data. Document as an explicit
  decision.
- Q: Migration of existing stored fingerprints? — Answer (assumed): version the
  fingerprint line so legacy reports are distinguishable; legacy → existing
  time-gate floor; no mass re-audit wave.

- Q (scope decision, 2026-10-21): The original trigger (unrelated whole-repo
  churn invalidating audits) was already fixed by SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P, so the
  strict item-data-only rule additionally removes per-touched-file protection
  (committed/uncommitted changes to files the item touched no longer
  invalidate), reversing tested behaviour shipped in SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P /
  SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ. — Answer (Map, on behalf of producer): "a" — proceed
  with the strict item-data-only formula (title + description only, zero git
  calls), as originally recorded; per-touched-path invalidation tests are
  rewritten to the new rule. Source: comment SA-C0MVIAGIQU003WW4P (reply to
  comment SA-C0MVI9Q5L3008NBLW). Research: inspected
  `_compute_content_fingerprint`/`_check_audit_freshness`/
  `_extract_content_fingerprint` at HEAD `fe85415a3`; confirmed whole-repo HEAD
  and `_resolve_working_tree_hash` are gone and the payload is
  `{path_states, description_hash, key_files}`; confirmed per-touched-path
  invalidation tests exist in `test_audit_runner_freshness.py`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVAWFJXM0096FAB** – Child freshness fingerprint test coverage (completed)
- **SA-0MVAWFYKT002CQ3L** – Stabilise child freshness fingerprint comments (completed)
- **SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT** – Audit: content-based freshness gate (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mskb6us1009cnht, 0msn04x2s006onh0, 0mspzdalb000s18p, 0msq026t3009qy2l, 0msq32mf200675ar (+356 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mskb6us1009cnht, 0msn04x2s006onh0, 0mspzdalb000s18p, 0msq026t3009qy2l, 0msq32mf200675ar (+335 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: 0mskb6us1009cnht, 0msl1yxg7004f2bz, 0mspzdalb000s18p, 0msq026t3009qy2l, 0mthc710x003orzm (+305 more)


## Plan

Decomposed 2026-10-21 (plan skill, Session herdr-1792601836-949358-7572).

Tenet: the parent's strict rule (item data only, zero git calls) re-touches child
reuse, the read-only probe and the ship consumer, so the decomposition keeps every
consumer working against the simplified formula rather than re-designing them.
Code + test migration land in one commit (the repo gate forbids a red commit), so
the test item is created first (test-first creation order) but executed after the
implementation item (blocking edge); its roll is the AC8 "nothing silently dropped"
ledger + mutation-style guards for the new contract.

| # | Child | Type | Priority | Depends on | Summary |
|---|-------|------|----------|-----------|---------|
| 1 | Verify item-data-only audit freshness contract (SA-0MVIDI6EL002E163) | task (test) | high | 2, 4 | Rewrites the per-touched-path/comment invalidation tests to assert the NEW rule (touched-file edits, HEAD moves, comments, lifecycle fields do not invalidate; title/description/Key-Files changes do), adds a zero-git-call guard + exact-payload test, versioned-line legacy fallback tests, and records a migrated-test ledger (parent AC8). |
| 2 | Fingerprint from item data only, v2 line (SA-0MVIDI8E00063OOP) | feature | high | — | Core slice: `_compute_content_fingerprint` hashes `{schema:2, title_hash, description_hash}` with zero git calls; versioned `Audit content fingerprint (v2): ` line; legacy unversioned reports fall back to the time gate; comments param removed at all call sites; TDD test migration in the same commit; docstrings updated. |
| 3 | Remove dead fingerprint git/comment machinery (SA-0MVIDIAAN002UCX6) | task | medium | 2 | Deletes `_compute_path_fingerprints` and `_fetch_item_comments` (grep-verified dead), cleans the children-test scaffolding that patched them; keeps `_resolve_touched_files` (file-scope manifest) and `_resolve_audited_head`. |
| 4 | Ship gates accept versioned fingerprint line (SA-0MVIDICGZ0030DXC) | task | high | — (same release as 2) | Updates the mirrored prefix + `hasContentFingerprint()` in `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` so the release content-freshness fast path keeps working; legacy v1 lines fall back to the local time gate; unit tests extended. |
| 5 | Update freshness-gate documentation (SA-0MVIDIEB8003LFHL) | docs | medium | 2, 3, 4 | Rewrites the freshness-gate sections of `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` to the item-data-only / versioned-line / legacy-fallback contract, incl. the one-time legacy re-audit consequence and its pre-flight full-suite cache-gate interaction; stale-reference grep sweep. |

**Vertical phasing:** single slice (the change must not ship half-versioned — a v2
payload under an unversioned prefix would mass-re-audit), so all five items land in
one release; order within the release: 2 and 4 first (same commit window), then 3,
then 5, then 1 (verification last, blocked on 2 + 4). Each item is a vertical slice
of its own scope (code + tests + docs + evidence).

**Interview inputs (already settled at intake, not re-asked):** strict rule (a);
title+description only; keep key_files out of the payload (derivative of
description_hash — AC1 permits); versioned line chosen for migration; comments/
status/stage/priority/assignee/sortIndex never invalidate; herdr dispatcher and
ship `isAuditFresh` time-based consumers out of scope.

### Plan: changelog
- 2026-10-21T~18:10Z — plan skill: created 5 children (test-first creation order), wired blocking deps (1←{2,4}, 3←2, 5←{2,3,4}); appended this Plan block. Effort Small / risk Medium (effort_and_risk skill estimate below).

## Appendix: planning questions & answers
*(No new clarifying questions were required in the planning session — the intake
Appendix on this item already records the scope decisions (strict rule, migration
via versioned line, comment/lifecycle non-invalidation, 2026-10-21 option (a)).
Planning re-used those answers rather than re-asking.)*

discovered-from:RISE-0MVBEJ3S8006YFHK

## Problem

The implement skill's Step 9 'belt-and-suspenders' post-push verification (/skill:test against the dev checkout) can resolve to a **cache hit and execute zero fresh tests**, while still looking like a green verification.

Observed end-to-end on RISE-0MVBEJ3S8006YFHK:
1. implement.py finish runs the full suite (changed-scope, then --scope full) **inside the worktree**, stores green entries keyed by git state + scope in the per-repo test cache (2h TTL).
2. implement.py pushes from the worktree. In this repo the pre-push hook is a worklog-sync hook that exits 0 for worktrees (line ~80) — no test execution happens at push time.
3. The skill then says run /skill:test post-push. Because the cache key is git state + scope only, the main checkout's lookup at the same commit hits the entry stored by the finish gate. Both suite commands returned CACHED exit=0 — the final verification ran nothing.
4. Worse: the worktree environment can differ from the main checkout in ways the cache cannot see — on RISE-0MVBEJ3S8006YFHK the core submodule failed to clone in the worktree ('transport file not allowed') and was populated manually; node_modules is symlinked. A green run recorded in the worktree is not proof the canonical checkout passes.

## Desired behaviour

- The post-push verification step must either (a) execute a genuinely fresh run against the canonical checkout when the push originated in a worktree (or when env differs), or (b) be made explicitly targeted for narrow changes (--scope changed --force) instead of a bare /skill:test that is cache-servable.
- The cache key should include enough environment/worktree identity that a worktree-recorded run cannot satisfy a main-checkout verification, OR implement.py finish should record whether the push came from a worktree so the post-push step knows to force a refresh.
- Keep fast iteration cheap: for narrow, well-covered changes, a forced changed-scope run is acceptable post-push evidence; reserve forced full runs for broad/refactor changes or environment drift (submodules, node_modules).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — After implement.py finish pushes from a worktree, a post-push verification on the main checkout executes a fresh run (it cannot be served from the cache entry recorded inside the worktree) for the affected scope.
- AC2 — A bare /skill:test post-push no longer silently returns 'green' from a cache populated by an in-worktree finish gate without executing: either the step force-refreshes, or the implement skill's Step 9 is updated to specify an explicit scope/force invocation (and documents when a forced full run is required vs a targeted one).
- AC3 — The per-repo test cache key (or its consumer logic in run_tests.py / implement.py) captures worktree-vs-main-checkout identity (e.g. git common dir, worktree path, or submodule status) so an in-worktree run and a main-checkout run for the same commit produce distinct entries.
- AC4 — Fast iteration is preserved: targeted post-push runs (--scope changed --force) remain the default for narrow changes; the full forced suite runs only when the change is broad, a refactor, or environment drift (submodule/node_modules) is detected.
- AC5 — Documented in implement SKILL.md Step 9 (and audit skill F3/F4 notes where relevant) with the exact commands; regression test in tests/ where the cache layer is tested.

## Constraints

- Do not break existing 2h-TTL caching for the audit skill's read-only full-suite verification — it still needs to query cached full runs at the same commit.
- Pre-existing framework items may partially intersect: SA-0MVCF5SHU002WNYU (document pre-push bypass + verification recipe), SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG (live-repo guard + push timeout). Reconcile rather than duplicate.
- Target files (from the live symlink tree /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills -> /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill): skill/test_cache.py (cache key), skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py (scope/force), skill/implement/scripts/implement.py (push origin record / verification step), skill/implement/SKILL.md (Step 9 wording), skill/audit/SKILL.md (F3/F4 notes if needed).

## Evidence

- Final /skill:test on RISE-0MVBEJ3S8006YFHK: both suites reported CACHED exit=0 scope=full, i.e. no fresh execution.
- Worktree push: pre-push hook exits 0 for worktrees (saw line ~80 'exit 0' in .git/hooks/pre-push); submodule 'core' failed to clone in the worktree and was populated manually.

# Audit performance measurement harness and committed baseline

**Parent:** SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG — Audits take too long: investigate and speed up

## Goal (user story)

As an operator or release producer, I want a committed, reproducible measurement of
audit LLM call timing, so I can verify that a performance change actually helped
instead of guessing.

## Problem statement

Every audit log on this host contains `Per-call timing:` lines, but no committed tool
parses them. The parent brief's baseline (1,637 instrumented calls, 140.8 h total,
62 % of call time in Phase 1, ~18 % wasted on timeouts and JSON re-asks) was produced
ad hoc and cannot be reproduced or regression-gated.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 (parent):** `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` is committed. It parses `Per-call timing:` lines from `~/.audit_debug/` (configurable root) and prints the per-context table with columns: context, calls, total, p50, p90, max, and count-at-budget. Running it on this host reproduces the parent brief's baseline figures within expected variance (documented tolerance).
- **AC1 (parent):** The harness is covered by a unit test using a small fixture corpus of synthetic debug logs — the test is written before the parser logic (TDD) and asserts each aggregate column including the count-at-budget buckets (600 s, 900 s, 1,800 s).
- **AC2 (parent):** `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` records the measured baseline (calls, total hours, per-context breakdown, Phase 1 share, wasted share) together with the reproduction command and a stated single-item audit wall-clock target of **≤ 10 minutes** on a healthy proxy with no concurrent audits, which becomes the regression gate.
- **AC2 (parent):** The baseline document names the gate explicitly and is referenced from `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.
- The harness is read-only: it never writes to `~/.audit_debug/`, `.worklog/`, or the audit runner.
- UK English throughout.
- **Parent AC1 traceability:** a script `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` parses `Per-call timing:` lines from `~/.audit_debug/` and prints the per-context table (calls, total, p50, p90, max, count-at-budget); running it on this host reproduces the baseline in this brief within expected variance; it is covered by a unit test with a fixture corpus.
- **Parent AC2 traceability:** the measured baseline (1,637 calls / 140.8h / 62% Phase 1 / 18% wasted) is committed to `docs/dev/` and a small-item audit wall-clock target of **≤ 10 minutes** (healthy proxy, no concurrent audits) is stated and used as the regression gate.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Write `scripts/tests/test_measure_audit_performance.py` against a fixture corpus
   (5–8 synthetic logs spanning each context) — asserts table shape and aggregates.
2. Implement `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` with `--root`, `--context`,
   `--at-budget` CLI options and stable table output.
3. Run it on this host; record the output in `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md`
   with the mandated ≤ 10 min target and reproduction command.
4. Link the baseline doc from `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` — new harness
- `scripts/tests/test_measure_audit_performance.py` — new unit tests + fixture logs
- `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` — new baseline + target document
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — link to the baseline document

## Dependencies

None — this is the foundation slice; every other child depends on it.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the recorded `~/.audit_debug` corpus is representative (491 items,
  one host). The document records the host, date range and per-context counts so a
  different corpus is obviously different.
- **Risk:** debug logs may be pruned during the work; the fixture corpus makes the unit
  test independent of live logs while the baseline document pins the snapshot.

# Verify item-data-only audit freshness contract

**Parent:** SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0 (Simplify audit freshness: invalidate only on this work item's own data change)

**User story:** As an audit operator, I want independent, executable proof that a stored audit is invalidated *only* by a change to this work item's own audited data (title/description/ACs/Key Files), so that unrelated repository activity can never silently invalidate or (worse) mask a stale audit.

**Why a separate verification item:** the parent's AC8 requires that no existing coverage is silently dropped. This item owns that guarantee: it enumerates the old per-touched-path / comment-contribution contract, proves each case is now asserted the *new* way, and adds mutation-style guards that fail if any git- or comment-derived component is ever reintroduced.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Non-invalidation regression tests assert the fingerprint is **unchanged** across all three previously-invalidating conditions: (a) HEAD movement caused by another work item's commit, (b) uncommitted/untracked working-tree changes anywhere in the repo, (c) committed, staged or dirty changes **to a file this item itself touched** (the direct reversal of `test_fingerprint_changes_when_touched_file_committed_change` / `..._dirty` / `..._staged` and `test_tool_artefact_rewrite_invalidates`).
2. Invalidation regression tests assert the fingerprint **changes** when the item's title changes, when its description/ACs change, and when its `Key Files` section changes.
3. Non-invalidation tests assert the fingerprint is unchanged after: adding a comment (including a comment recording a commit hash), and changing `status` / `stage` / `priority` / `assignee` / `sortIndex` (all of which move `updatedAt`).
4. A mutation-style guard asserts `_compute_content_fingerprint` makes **zero** git calls: with the runner's git-executing helpers patched to raise, a fingerprint is still returned; and an exact-payload test asserts the hashed payload keys are exactly the item-data schema (no `path_states`, no `head`/`worktree`, no comment-derived keys), so reintroducing a component fails a test.
5. Versioned-line tests: the persisted report's `Audit content fingerprint (v2): <hex>` line round-trips through `_extract_content_fingerprint`; an unversioned legacy line (`Audit content fingerprint: <hex>`) makes `_extract_content_fingerprint` return `None` and the gate falls back to the time floor (fresh inside `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_BUFFER_SECONDS` + persist-write tolerance, stale beyond it); `check-freshness --json` reports `hasFingerprint: false` for a legacy v1 report and `true` for a v2 report.
6. Child-reuse coverage: `_get_child_audit_verdict` / `_child_content_changed` reuse a child whose own data is unchanged, and treat a title/description change as stale.
7. A ledger comment on this item lists **every** pre-existing freshness test that was rewritten, kept or removed, with the reason for each — so nothing is silently dropped (parent AC8).
8. `skill/audit/tests` and `skill/ship` unit tests pass via `/skill:test` (changed scope), with the verification evidence (test names + file:line) recorded in a comment.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` (`TestContentFreshnessGate` plus a new item-data-only class) and `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py`.
- Reuse the existing `_FakeGitRepo` / `mock.patch.object` fixtures; add the zero-git-call guard by patching the git-executing helper with a `RuntimeError`-raising stub.
- Record the migrated-test ledger as a `wl comment add` on this item.
- Run the changed-scope suite through `/skill:test`; do not invoke pytest directly.

## Constraints

- Tests only — no production behaviour changes in this item; any gap found is reported on the owning implementation item (SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0 children) rather than fixed here out of scope.
- Read-only: no `pi` calls, no full-audit pipeline execution needed.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` — migrated + new contract tests (zero-git guard, exact payload, versioned/legacy lines)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py` — probe `hasFingerprint` v2 vs legacy
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_children.py` — child-reuse freshness expectations
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — subject under verification (no changes in this item)

# Fingerprint from item data only, v2 line

**Parent:** SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0 (Simplify audit freshness: invalidate only on this work item's own data change)

**User story:** As an audit operator, I want the audit content fingerprint computed from this work item's own data only, with zero git calls, so an unrelated commit — or even a change to a file this item touched — never invalidates a stored audit.

**Producer decision (2026-10-21, comment SA-C0MVIAGIQU003WW4P):** option (a) — the strict item-data-only formula (title + description, zero git calls) supersedes the per-touched-path formula from SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P. This is the core slice of the parent item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_compute_content_fingerprint` hashes a canonical JSON payload of **exactly** `{"schema": 2, "title_hash": <sha256(title)>, "description_hash": <sha256(description)>}` (`sort_keys=True`, then sha256 hex of the serialised payload). No `path_states`, no `key_files`, no comment-derived input (the Key Files section is part of the description and therefore already covered by `description_hash`).
2. The computation performs **zero git invocations**: it does not call `_resolve_touched_files`, `_compute_path_fingerprints` or any `git` subprocess, and is correspondingly fast (no repo probing) — asserted by a test that patches the git-executing helpers to raise.
3. `_compute_content_fingerprint` returns `None` (fail open → full re-audit) only when the work item cannot be fetched (`wl show` failure) or the payload cannot be built; a missing/garbage description still yields a deterministic hash.
4. `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX` becomes the **versioned** `"Audit content fingerprint (v2): "`; `_extract_content_fingerprint` returns a value only for `v2` lines and returns `None` for unversioned legacy lines, so legacy reports fall through to the existing time-gate floor (`AUDIT_FRESHNESS_BUFFER_SECONDS` + persist-write tolerance) with **no silent mass re-audit wave**. All three persist sites (~5714, ~5740, ~6158) emit the versioned line.
5. The now-unused `comments` parameter of `_compute_content_fingerprint` is removed and every call site updated: `_check_audit_freshness` (~2020), `_get_child_audit_verdict` (~6606), `_run_remediation_loop` (~10171), `_phase_fetch_and_cq` (~10357), `_reaudit_budget_exceeded_children` (~10786), `_phase_children` (~11516, ~11918). `cmd_check_freshness` (~2117/2120) keeps working and reports `hasFingerprint` from the versioned line.
6. **TDD, same commit:** the per-touched-path and comment-contribution invalidation tests are rewritten to assert the new rule *before* the behaviour change, and the change lands only when `skill/audit/tests` is green — the repo gate forbids a red commit, so code + test migration are one commit (`<WIP-id>: <summary>` recorded on this item).
7. Docstrings on `_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_check_audit_freshness`, `_extract_content_fingerprint` and `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX` describe the item-data-only, zero-git, versioned-line contract; no docstring still claims path/worktree/comment components.
8. Verdict semantics unchanged: `--force` still bypasses the gate; the freshness skip still returns the stored `rawOutput` verbatim (an explicit `Ready to close: No` is never masked).

## Minimal implementation

- Rewrite `_compute_content_fingerprint` in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` to the item-data-only payload; drop the `comments` parameter and its plumbing.
- Version the prefix constant and make `_extract_content_fingerprint` version-aware (v2 only; legacy → `None`).
- Migrate the affected tests in `test_audit_runner_freshness.py`, `test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py`, `test_no_breakage_chore.py`, `test_audit_runner_remediation.py` (literal-prefix assertions → the v2 constant).
- Keep `_resolve_touched_files` untouched (still used by the Phase-2 file-scope manifest at ~5257/~7964/~10897); dead-code removal is a separate item.

## Constraints

- Read-only: no test-suite execution or `pi` calls from the fingerprint path.
- Do not re-design the consumers (child reuse, read-only probe, ship `isAuditFresh`) — they must keep working against the simplified formula, not be extended.
- Documented trade-off (accepted): a stored audit may reference code that later changed, including files this item touched. The audit verdict remains the record for the item's own data.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_compute_content_fingerprint`, `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`, `_extract_content_fingerprint`, `_check_audit_freshness`, persist sites, call sites
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` — rule migration
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py` — probe expectations
- `skill/audit/tests/test_no_breakage_chore.py` — literal prefix assertions
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_remediation.py` — literal prefix assertion

# Remove dead fingerprint git/comment machinery

**Parent:** SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0 (Simplify audit freshness: invalidate only on this work item's own data change)

**User story:** As a maintainer, I want the git/comment machinery that only the old fingerprint needed removed, so the freshness path is smaller and no future change can quietly resurrect a repo-state component.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_compute_path_fingerprints` (~2336) is deleted once it has no callers; the tests whose only subject was that helper (`test_compute_path_fingerprints_*`, `TestTouchedFileResolution` ~311-344 in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py`) are removed with a note in the item ledger comment (`_FakeGitRepo` usage reviewed — keep only what other tests still need).
2. `_fetch_item_comments` (~2163) is deleted if it has no remaining callers (it existed to make the fingerprint's comment contribution deterministic); if any caller remains, it must be named in the item comment with the reason it stays.
3. `_resolve_touched_files` (~2213) and `_compute_path_fingerprints`'s sibling helpers are **retained** where still used by the Phase-2 file-scope manifest (~5257, ~7964, ~10897) and their tests stay green; `_resolve_audited_head` (~2852) is retained for green-run attestation.
4. Test scaffolding that patched the removed helpers is cleaned up: the `_deterministic_fingerprint` autouse fixture and `_DEFAULT_STATES` / `_DEFAULT_TOUCHED` constants and the `states=` parameter of `_fingerprinted_raw` in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_children.py`. Fixtures that remain must express the item-data-only contract, not a pinned path state.
5. Grep evidence recorded in an item comment: no reference to the removed symbols remains in `skill/audit/**`, `skill/ship/**` or `scripts/**` (excluding the docs owned by the documentation item), and `python3 -m compileall` / import of the audit runner succeeds.
6. `/skill:test` changed-scope run is green after the deletion.

## Minimal implementation

- Delete the dead functions and their now-obsolete tests; update the children-test fixtures to the simplified contract.
- Confirm each deletion with a grep, then run the changed-scope suite via `/skill:test`.

## Constraints

- Surgical: do not refactor the retained file-scope manifest path.
- A helper is only removed when a grep proves it has no production caller.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — delete `_compute_path_fingerprints` / `_fetch_item_comments`; keep `_resolve_touched_files`, `_resolve_audited_head`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` — remove helper-only tests
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_children.py` — remove `_deterministic_fingerprint` / `_DEFAULT_STATES` scaffolding

# Ship gates accept versioned fingerprint line

**Parent:** SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0 (Simplify audit freshness: invalidate only on this work item's own data change)

**User story:** As a release operator, I want the ship audit gates to recognise the new versioned content-fingerprint line, so the content-freshness fast path keeps working after the fingerprint is versioned.

**Context:** `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` mirrors the runner's prefix (`AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX = 'Audit content fingerprint: '`) and detects fingerprint-bearing audits with `haystack.includes(...)` (~line 478) to decide whether to spawn the read-only `check-freshness` probe (`queryContentFreshness`, SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI). Once the runner writes `Audit content fingerprint (v2): <hex>`, that `includes()` check silently fails and every audited item falls back to the local time gate — fail-safe but a regression of the release fast path.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX` in `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` is updated to the versioned `'Audit content fingerprint (v2): '` (or `hasContentFingerprint` is made version-aware), so a v2-bearing audit is detected and the probe path is taken.
2. `hasContentFingerprint()` returns `false` for legacy unversioned (`Audit content fingerprint: <hex>`) reports — those correctly fall back to the local time gate instead of spawning a probe that would only reproduce the time gate — and `false` for fingerprint-less reports; `true` for v2 reports in both `audit.rawOutput` and `audit.summary`.
3. `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs` covers v2-present, legacy-v1-present and absent cases, and the existing `check-final-validation.js` consumer (`classification.kind === 'stale' && hasContentFingerprint(auditData)`) still routes stale+v2 audits to the probe.
4. Ship unit tests for the audit gate pass via `/skill:test` (`tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`, `tests/unit/test-ship-scripts.mjs`).
5. Sequencing note recorded: this item should land in the same release as the fingerprint change; if it lands later, the intervening window is fail-safe (extra re-audits, no incorrect passes).

## Minimal implementation

- Update the mirrored prefix constant and `hasContentFingerprint()` (plus its docstring) in `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`.
- Extend `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs` with the three cases.
- No change to `queryContentFreshness` / `audit-freshness.js` behaviour.

## Constraints

- Read-only gate code: no new spawns, no behavioural change to verdict semantics.
- The herdr dispatcher-side `isAuditFresh` (ContextHub repo) is out of scope.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`, `hasContentFingerprint()`
- `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs` — v2 / legacy / absent cases
- `tests/unit/test-ship-scripts.mjs` — gate regression expectations

# Update freshness-gate documentation

**Parent:** SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0 (Simplify audit freshness: invalidate only on this work item's own data change)

**User story:** As an agent or operator reading the audit docs, I want the documented freshness rule to match the shipped code — item data only, versioned line, legacy fallback — so I do not design around a per-touched-file gate that no longer exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` freshness-gate section (~248-318, plus the re-audit-coordination bullets ~579-594 and the child-reuse mentions ~699/816) is rewritten to the new contract: the content fingerprint covers the work item's **own data only** (title + description, which contains the ACs and Key Files), with **zero git calls**; unrelated commits, working-tree churn, changes to files the item touched, comments, and lifecycle-field changes do **not** invalidate; description/title/AC/Key-Files changes do.
2. The same file documents the **versioned line** (`Audit content fingerprint (v2): <sha256hex>`), the legacy/unversioned fallback to the time-gate floor, and the resulting one-time re-audit consequence for legacy in-review items whose `updatedAt` moved after their audit — including its interaction with the pre-flight full-suite cache gate (a re-audit of a legacy item can block on the cache gate, the exact failure seen on SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0).
3. The documented trade-off is explicit: dropping the per-path components means a stored audit may reference code that changed under it (protection deliberately added by SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ and SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P is removed by producer decision, comment SA-C0MVIAGIQU003WW4P).
4. `skill/audit/SKILL.md` freshness-gate summary (~42, ~182-186, ~204-210) is updated consistently, including the child-reuse wording (children use the same simplified fingerprint: unchanged child data → reused).
5. `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` (~197) is updated to the v2 prefix so the ship fast-path description matches the mirror constant.
6. Stale-reference sweep recorded in an item comment: `grep -rn "per-touched-file\|path_states\|comment-recorded commit\|Comment-consistency contract" docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md skill/audit/SKILL.md skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` returns only intentional historical/decision notes.
7. Documentation-related tests pass via `/skill:test` (`skill/audit/tests/test_skill_md_and_debug_logs.py` and ship unit tests).

## Minimal implementation

- Rewrite the freshness-gate section of `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (content gate, fallback, fail-open, `--force`, trade-off, migration note).
- Update the `skill/audit/SKILL.md` summary lines and the ship reference line.
- Run the grep sweep and record the result.

## Constraints

- Documentation only — no code changes in this item; discrepancies found in code are reported on the owning implementation item.
- Keep the docs' existing structure/headings so inbound links and cross-references stay valid.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — freshness-gate section
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — freshness-gate summary lines
- `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — content-fingerprint fast-path paragraph
